requirements.text: The Clarus system shall implement quality checking processes as soon as data become available.
The Clarus system shall record the methods applied when deriving quality checking information.
The Clarus system shall be able to implement quality checking rules for each environmental parameter.
The Clarus system shall be able to implement quality checking rules for specific environmental situations.
The Clarus system shall be able to implement quality checking rules specific to observation locations.
The Clarus system shall be able to base its quality checking process on historical environmental data.
The Clarus system shall be able to use multiple algorithms for its quality checking process.
The Clarus system shall allow access to new surface transportation-related environmental data.
The Clarus system shall enable administrators to manage security groups.
The Clarus system shall be able to restrict environmental data publication based on source.
The Clarus system shall record statistics about its operation.
The Clarus system shall log data transactions.
The Clarus system shall acquire, process, and disseminate environmental metadata.
The Clarus system shall manage environmental data and metadata according to the Clarus data sharing agreements.
The Clarus system shall collect, quality check, and disseminate environmental data.
The Clarus system shall provide environmental data quality flags.
The Clarus system shall allow human quality checks of environmental data.
The Clarus system shall provide a user interface for administration.
The Clarus system shall be able to detect data submission errors.
The Clarus system shall be able to access in-situ environmental observations from data collectors.
The Clarus system shall be able to access remotely sensed environmental observations from data collectors.
The Clarus system shall be able to receive roadway weather measurements derived from VII data.
The Clarus system shall accept environmental data derived from images.
The Clarus system shall be able to retrieve environmental data directly from environmental sensor station collectors.
The Clarus system shall minimize the time for data acquisition.
The Clarus system shall process data as they are received.
The Clarus system shall collect pavement-related observations.
The Clarus system shall accept environmental data from railway systems or in-situ ESS along tracks.
The Clarus system shall accept environmental data from railroad vehicles.
The Clarus system shall accept environmental data from (roadway) vehicles.
The Clarus system shall accept environmental data from maintenance and construction vehicles.
The Clarus system shall accept environmental data from service patrol vehicles.
The Clarus system shall accept environmental data from transit vehicles.
The Clarus system shall accept environmental data from emergency vehicles.
The Clarus system shall be able to receive weather data from weather service providers.
The Clarus system baseline data types shall be defined by the NTCIP ESS 1204 standard.
The Clarus system data definitions shall be consistent with the ITE TM 1.03 standard, Functional Level Traffic Management Data Dictionary (TMDD).
The Clarus system shall acquire, process, and disseminate environmental data.
The system shall implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to manage user permissions and enforce the principle of least privilege for all administrative and data access functions.
The system shall maintain immutable, time-stamped audit logs of all data transactions and administrative actions, protected against unauthorized deletion or modification for a minimum of 12 months.
The Clarus system shall acquire environmental data from collectors with an average end-to-end latency of less than 5 seconds.
The Clarus system shall maintain an operational availability of 99.9% during peak traffic hours.

Upon detection of a data submission error, the system shall log the error, notify the administrator, and automatically quarantine the malformed data packet without interrupting the processing of valid data.
The system shall achieve an average end-to-end latency of less than 30 seconds for 95% of environmental data observations from receipt at the collector to availability in the QEDC.
The system shall process and make available 99% of incoming data within 5 seconds of receipt under a peak load of 10,000 observations per second.

OPEN: The PRD mentions 'data sharing agreements' and 'redistribution restrictions' but lacks requirements for data encryption in transit or at rest. - All environmental data and metadata transmitted to or from the Clarus system shall be encrypted using industry-standard protocols (e.g., TLS 1.2+).

OPEN: The PRD does not specify requirements for input validation or sanitization of data received from external collectors. - The system shall perform strict input validation and sanitization on all incoming environmental data and metadata to prevent injection attacks and ensure data integrity.

OPEN: The PRD does not specify the expected volume of data or the number of concurrent data providers/consumers. - The Clarus system shall support the ingestion of data from at least 10,000 concurrent environmental sensor stations and provide data to at least 500 concurrent service provider connections.

OPEN: The PRD mentions the system must handle a 'vast range of data' and 'large volumes' but provides no specific throughput or capacity requirements (e.g., observations per second, number of concurrent sensor stations). - The system shall support a sustained throughput of at least 10,000 observations per second and a total capacity of 50,000 concurrent environmental sensor stations.
